statement: Nitrate concentration in the mobile water of a soil layer
equation: conc_NO3,mobile = NO3_ly * (1 - exp(-w_mobile / ((1 - theta_e) * SAT_ly))) / w_mobile
variables: NO3_ly: nitrate in the layer (kg N/ha); w_mobile: mobile water, sum of surface runoff, lateral flow and percolation (mm); theta_e: fraction of porosity from which anions are excluded (SWAT+ input ANION_EXCL); SAT_ly: saturated water content of the layer (mm)
note: Page lists the unit of conc as kg N/mm H2O; dividing kg N/ha by mm gives kg N/(ha mm), so that unit is a simplification

statement: Nitrate moved to the layer below by percolation
variables: w_perc,ly: water percolating to the underlying layer on that day (mm); NO3_perc,ly: nitrate moved down (kg N/ha)

statement: The plan's mixing model 'N pool x drainage / soil water volume' is the first-order form of the SWAT+ equations
equation: for small w_mobile, 1 - exp(-x) ~ x, so conc ~ NO3_ly / ((1 - theta_e) * SAT_ly) and NO3_perc ~ NO3_ly * w_perc / ((1 - theta_e) * SAT_ly)
variables: the 'soil water volume' of the plan = (1 - theta_e) * SAT_ly, the pore water volume in which anions can move (mm)
source: derived from the two SWAT+ equations above (series expansion, not stated in the source)
note: Needs a cap: with large drainage the linear form can exceed the pool, the exponential form cannot. Prefer the exact equation. theta_e and SAT_ly are not in the repo yet: SAT_ly from SSURGO water content, theta_e (ANION_EXCL) default not retrieved

statement: K-State credits 20 lb N/ac per 1 % soil organic matter in its N recommendation
equation: N = (ie/fe)*EY - se*ProfileN - SOM*20 - ManureN - OtherN + PreviousCropAdj
variables: SOM: soil organic matter (%); EY: expected yield (bu/ac); result in lb N/ac
source: K-State Research and Extension, MF2586 (Ruiz Diaz, Jan 2024), p. 5
note: a credit in a fertilizer recommendation, not a measured mineralization rate

statement: UNL credits soil organic matter as 0.14 times the yield goal per 1 % OM, up to 3 % OM
equation: credit = 0.14 * %OM(max 3) * yield_goal  (28 lb N/ac per 1 % OM at 200 bu/ac)
variables: example, irrigated, 200 bu/ac, no nitrate credit: 197, 169, 141, 113 lb N/ac at 0, 1, 2, 3 % OM
source: University of Nebraska-Lincoln CropWatch, Credit Soil Organic Matter for Nitrogen
note: scales with the yield goal: 14 lb N/ac per 1 % OM at 100 bu/ac. Gives the low and high ends of the sensitivity

statement: Typical growing-season N mineralization in the 0-6 in topsoil is 15 to 50 kg/ha (13.5 to 44.5 lb/ac), an estimate
equation: worked example on the page: 5 % OM topsoil holds 0.25 % total N; if 1 % of it mineralizes in the season, about 50 kg N/ha
variables: range for the Canadian prairie; high-OM soils under long-term no-till with legumes can exceed 50 kg/ha
source: Top Crop Manager, 'Understanding N mineralization', quoting J. Schoenau (University of Saskatchewan)
note: secondary source, used as a plausibility check only. The field estimate 21-42 lb N/ac (1.5 % OM) lies inside it
